dispositions.reason: Step 5 must parse the amount with the existing parseMinor() and compare remaining in integer minor units (formatMinor for output), not parseFloat/dollars; this conflicts with the SPEC money constraint and with the plan's own steps 8-9.
Step 2 must update the existing version-1 migration case in test/store.test.js to expect schemaVersion 3 (plus the new refunds/refundKeys defaults) instead of keeping it unchanged.

Step 7 must require an own-property check (Object.hasOwn) or a null-prototype/Map structure for refundKeys so keys like constructor or __proto__ cannot hit inherited properties; the migration default must match.
The plan leans on an AC-TESTS.md that is absent although the SPEC is templated; the re-plan must produce it (or stop citing it) so every AC has a mapped test before the build.
Listing refunds is in the SPEC scope but has no planned test; the plan must add a test for GET /invoices/:id/refunds covering org scoping, order and the role it chooses.
The plan cites a README upgrade line that does not exist; step 11 must add the forward-only v3 note to the README (or the Risks text must stop claiming it).
Step 11 should also document the Idempotency-Key contract in the README: per-invoice scope, 200 on replay, original refund returned regardless of body, keys never expire.
Step 6 must place key-format, reason and non-string amount/reason validation in the order of checks so the error a multi-defect request gets is fixed by the plan, not guessed in the build.

Cannot tell whether a reused key with a different amount should replay or be rejected; the SPEC states only same-request retry. Re-plan should surface this for a recorded decision rather than let the build assume.
Step 10 must say how headers reach the handler and how the route learns a result was a replay (the result shape must carry it past presentRefund) so the 200/201 choice is buildable as written.
Acceptance mapping needs tests for the new 422 codes and the exact-remaining boundary from the SPEC scenario (refund the last 70.00, a third attempt refused).
The SPEC asks for an audit entry for every recorded refund only; the service has no logging layer, so observability of refused attempts is outside this SPEC and not needed by the build.
The SPEC does not choose who may list refunds or read reasons; the plan picked member role alone. Re-plan should justify or tighten the role so the decision is recorded.
The Risks section should state that the no-double-refund argument assumes a single process owning the data file; a one-line plan edit while re-planning.
The 1-100 printable-ASCII key bound is stated in step 7 and nothing in the SPEC contradicts it; a missing rationale does not stop the build.
